caseSummaries.title: Fiber access: ownership, permits and service
caseSummaries.storySummary: Fiber internet is being developed in Pueblo. Intrepid's local project page identifies T-Fiber as an ordering partner and distinguishes planned construction, engineering and permitting, construction, and service availability. Those stages matter: a fiber line in the neighborhood does not mean an individual address can order service.
storyLinks: Intrepid Pueblo project and ordering information

caseSummaries.title: Library AI: contracts, privacy, costs and useful outcomes
caseSummaries.storySummary: Pueblo City-County Library District announced a partnership with BoodleBox in its September 2026 program guide, with library staff training first and a September 22 public launch program. This is a real local example of AI literacy moving into a public institution. It does not establish that every patron receives an account or that a particular paid subscription is included.
storyLinks: Learn and use AI in Pueblo

caseSummaries.title: Library finance: audited records, services and facility use
caseSummaries.storySummary: The library's November 10 preliminary 2027 budget projects General Fund revenue of $17.44 million, spending of $16.00 million, and a $2.15 million transfer to its capital project fund. Its projected General Fund balance declines from an estimated $5.64 million at the end of 2026 to $4.93 million at the end of 2027—a decrease of roughly $705,000. The capital fund balance moves in the opposite direction, so these figures must not be added as independent spending.
storyLinks: November 10 preliminary budget, narrative and fund tables

caseSummaries.title: Passenger rail: station plans, owners and service commitments
caseSummaries.storySummary: Passenger rail planning connects a proposed service with local station access, host railroads, district governance and funding. The Front Range Passenger Rail District describes its delivery plan and a November 3 ballot question. It specifically directs readers to aggregated results across all twelve participating counties.
storyLinks: Rail district delivery plan and election information

caseSummaries.title: Railroad-tie fire: evidence, material and jurisdiction questions
caseSummaries.storySummary: The archived case concerns a reported September 5 railroad-tie fire in Pueblo's Midtown area. The earlier research names municipal fire and code functions along with environmental agencies. The linked September news accounts describe the incident; federal reference material explains creosote generally, not the specific materials or exposure at this site.

caseSummaries.title: School authorization and governance: roles and public records
caseSummaries.storySummary: School governance determines who authorizes a school, administers its operations, receives funds and is accountable for student services. An online school authorization can differ from a local district's responsibilities. Earlier Pueblo research identifies Riverstone Academy, Education reEnvisioned BOCES, District 70 and state education records as distinct leads.
storyLinks: Colorado Department of Education authorization announcement

caseSummaries.title: Connecting Communities: trail funding and delivery
caseSummaries.storySummary: Connecting Communities trail planning concerns how people might travel between neighborhoods and public destinations. The archived research identifies regional planning, City and County participation, a transportation funding record and an April 2026 design solicitation.

caseSummaries.title: Wastewater: incident, repair and public-health clearance
caseSummaries.storySummary: Pueblo's September 14 statement describes its account of an August wastewater release into the Arkansas River, detection and bypass repair. The event connects utility operations with downstream public health and environmental oversight.
